newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain-Corn offers slip but HRW values up.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain-Corn offers slip but HRW values up.

text.p: U.S. FOB Gulf corn offers slipped one cent a bushel in most positions on Monday while hard red winter wheat offers rose, dealers said.
"The (HRW) FOB offers are up so they can be out of the potential range of trading until people can get a feel of what kind of specs they can offer," one exporter said.
Wheat prices soared after freezing temperatures clamped down on the developing winter crop in the U.S., threatening to cut both production and exports this year, analysts said.
The market was waiting to see much hard red winter wheat was damaged by a recent freeze, he said.
These offers that are being raised were "a precautionary measure," the dealer said.

Readings dipped into the teens Fahrenheit over the weekend from Kansas into Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle, where winter wheat planted last fall has been emerging from dormancy to start forming new leaves.

Also, high water levels continued to plague barge traffic on the upper Mississippi. The U.S. Coast Guard on Monday imposed navigation restrictions on the port of St Louis due to rising water. Swift currents and rough weather played a part in several accidents on the lower Mississippi over the weekend.
